_comment: Registry of upstream data sources for the OurHike pipeline. Generated/updated by discover_sources.py - re-run that script rather than hand-editing urls here. A source discovery cannot see, because it is not an ArcGIS layer behind the Experience Builder app, is registered by hand and marked with a `kind`: discover_sources.py keeps entries it did not rediscover verbatim, so a hand-written entry survives a re-run. lib/source_registry.py is what reads `kind`, and an entry without one is an ArcGIS feature layer.

photo_licence._comment: The basis on which the Photo1..Photo10 images on the ATC facilities layers may be mirrored and served, recorded rather than assumed - CONTRIBUTING.md, 'A note on data and licences'. This is NOT a Creative Commons grant and must not be rendered as one: ATC holds the copyright, and what is recorded here is the permission to use them, not a licence to sublicense them onward. A club inheriting this project needs to re-confirm it in its own name rather than relying on this line.
photo_licence.author: Appalachian Trail Conservancy
photo_licence.basis: Maintainer authorisation, on the basis of Appalachian Trail Conservancy affiliation
photo_licence.open_question: https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/98 - ATC's redistribution and attribution terms are unresolved in general, and settling them should replace this line with the agreed terms.

atc_licence._comment: The basis on which DATA the Appalachian Trail Conservancy publishes on its own ArcGIS org and services may be reused - photo_licence's sibling, extended from the photos to the data layers by the maintainer's declaration of 2026-08-13 ('anything from the ATC is reusable', restated specifically for the FarOut-measured CSI water distances - #688). Scope, stated tightly: facts ATC itself publishes (half-mile points, the Campsite_Sustainability_Index water distances build_water_distance.py takes, whatever future ATC-org layer a change deliberately adopts). It does NOT cover documents the maintaining clubs publish (per-entry licence fields govern those, e.g. gatc_water_sources below), does NOT override editorial holdbacks that are about safety or partnership rather than licensing (CSI's user-created campsites stay unpublished - SOURCE_SURVEY.md §3b), and is not a grant to sublicense ATC's work onward.
atc_licence.author: Appalachian Trail Conservancy
atc_licence.basis: Maintainer authorisation, on the basis of Appalachian Trail Conservancy affiliation
atc_licence.open_question: ATC's own written terms remain the ideal - SOURCE_SURVEY.md §10's combined ask (capacity, Helene status, CSI, half-mile points) is now a confirmation rather than a blocker, and its answer should replace this line, the same way photo_licence's open question reads.

sources.title: A.T. Trail Updates
sources.licence: Facts and a link only, and NOT a grant to mirror ATC's prose. What is published is the mile range, category, states, headline and ATC's own last-updated date, with a link back to their page - facts about the trail, which is a different thing from the paragraphs ATC wrote about them. #458 asked ATC directly what may be republished and was closed without asking, on the maintainer's judgement as an ATC trail volunteer; that decision settles the conservative version and not the broader one, so the body text stays on ATC's own page. A club inheriting this project needs to confirm this in its own name rather than relying on this line - the same footing as `photo_licence` above and the general question in https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/98.

freshness.notes: The RSS feed, used as a change signal and NOT as the content. Measured 2026-08-24: it held 3 items while the listing held 89 across ten paginated pages, so building the artifact from it would silently drop the most consequential closure (features/ATC_TRAIL_UPDATES.md, 'what the feed does not carry'). The 2026-08-09 version of this note read '3 items while the page showed 9'; the 9 was page one mistaken for the whole list, which is https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/945. It does carry an ETag that moves when ATC edits, which is all a freshness marker needs - WEAK (`W/"..."`) as measured 2026-08-24, where this note said 'strong' on 2026-08-12; check_freshness.py compares it verbatim and only asks whether it moved, but a weak validator lets the upstream change the bytes without changing the tag. The listing page itself is still not usable as the marker, and now for two reasons. The correction this note carried briefly on 2026-08-24 - 'it no longer 403s a scripted request, it answers 200' - was measured with curl and did not describe the pipeline's own client: re-measured the same day, ATC refuses the literal `python-requests/*` User-Agent with 403 and answers 200 to curl and to a named agent, so the original 2026-08-12 finding was right about check_freshness.py and still is. lib/atc_scrape.py reaches the listing only because it sets a User-Agent naming the project. On top of that, a HEAD on the listing returns neither an ETag nor a Last-Modified, so even an allowed request would give a marker of UNKNOWN forever.

sources.discovered_via: features/ATC_TRAIL_UPDATES.md - read from ATC's public website, not from an ArcGIS service. Registered by hand because discover_sources.py walks the Experience Builder app and this source is not in it.
sources.notes: Not fetched by fetch_all.py and has no data/raw/<key>.geojson - the build input is the reviewed file named in `reviewed_input`, which a human edits and a merged pull request releases (#460). The freshness marker is what tells that human ATC has published something since they last looked.

sources.title: GATC Water Sources (approach trail + Georgia A.T.)
sources.licence: Unstated - a free public download from GATC's own site, fetched for REVIEW AND CROSS-CHECKS ONLY. Nothing from this source reaches a published artifact until GATC answers a redistribution ask (CONTRIBUTING.md, 'A note on data and licences'; the ask is the same shape as https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/98 records for opentrail.org). WATER_SOURCES.md §4 sizes this document as 'a pilot-state candidate after an email' and notes its embedded title is 'GATC Water Update July 2020.xlsx', so the 2026-03 file may re-export older data - a second reason the ask precedes any publication.
sources.discovered_via: SOURCE_SURVEY.md §5's club sweep (the 'water-sources PDF (2026-03-02)' row); fetched and parsed live 2026-08-13 (#669). Registered by hand - discover_sources.py walks the Experience Builder app and this source is not in it.
sources.notes: Fetched by fetch_club_pdfs.py to data/raw/club_pdfs/<key>.pdf (never by fetch_all.py), parsed by lib/club_pdfs.py to <key>.json beside it: 65 rows (4 approach trail + 61 A.T., measured on the live PDF 2026-08-13, agreeing with WATER_SOURCES.md §4's count) of GATC mile point + entry text. The PDF's text layer stores each printed row as one string, so the 'Source Name' and 'Distance Off AT' columns arrive fused and are kept that way rather than split by guesswork - lib/club_pdfs.py's docstring holds the measurement.

sources.title: OSM water point sources (fourteen A.T. states)
sources.licence: ODbL 1.0 - attribution and share-alike, the terms the self-built basemap already complies with; the client's credits screen names OpenStreetMap and each published water point's description carries 'Mapped by OpenStreetMap contributors'. This is the openly licensed half of #529's water answer - no ask pending, unlike the ATC and club rows above.
sources.discovered_via: WATER_SOURCES.md's census for #529 (spike_osm_water_census.py) measured OSM point sources within 250 m of 26% of shelters trail-wide and 40% in the south, against 8% for the shipped supply. Registered by hand - discover_sources.py walks the Experience Builder app and this source is not in it.
sources.notes: Fetched by fetch_osm_water.py to data/raw/osm_water.geojson (never by fetch_all.py): nodes tagged natural=spring, amenity=drinking_water, man_made=water_tap or man_made=water_well across the fourteen Geofabrik state extracts export_basemap.py already downloads - 7,574 nodes on the first full scan (2026-08-13). No freshness entry on purpose: Geofabrik republishes the extracts daily, so a changed-marker would always say yes (export_basemap.py's docstring holds the reasoning; the fetch is skip-if-present with --refetch). export_poi.py folds these into poi_type water at low confidence, dropping each point within 25 m of an opentrail water point as the same node arriving twice.

sources.title: 3D Hydrography Program (3DHP)
sources.licence: Public domain, as a work of the United States government — the whole USGS hydrography column (WATER_SOURCES.md §5). Attribution is courtesy rather than obligation, and the client's credits screen already names USGS for NHD.

freshness.notes: The distinct `workunitid` values 3DHP's flowline layer returns for boxes on the trail. `NHD` is 3DHP saying, in its own field, that these lines are the retired dataset republished rather than anything it has surveyed - measured 2026-08-14 at five points spread along the trail from North Carolina (mile 110) to New Hampshire (mile 1,868), every one of them `NHD`. When that stops being the answer, 3DHP has resurveyed the corridor and the migration this pipeline is deliberately not doing becomes worth costing. Changing `recorded` is how a person acknowledges having looked; nothing writes it automatically.

sources.discovered_via: WATER_SOURCES.md §5, following USGS's retirement of the NHD on 2023-10-01. Registered by hand - discover_sources.py walks ATC's Experience Builder app and this is not in it.
sources.notes: Nothing fetches this. It is registered because the pipeline's water derivation (fetch_trail_water.py) reads a dataset USGS no longer maintains, and this is where its replacement will appear. Measured 2026-08-14: for the corridor, 3DHP IS NHD - identical geometry (1,265 flowlines in a box in central Virginia against NHD's 1,265, same vertex count, worst-case separation 0.086 mm) and identical springs (1,796 features, every one within 1 m of an NHD spring) - with the perennial/intermittent FCode collapsed away into an undifferentiated `Channel Line`. Migrating now would trade the only structured seasonality signal the pipeline has for the same geometry, so the entry holds a watch instead of a fetch.

A USDM week runs Tuesday to Monday and is released on the Thursday, so the fetcher walks back a week at a time - a midweek 404 is 'not published yet', not a failure. export_drought.py clips to a 10 km corridor (27.6 MB national file to about 10 KB gzipped, losslessly - WATER_CONDITIONS.md §4), un-nests the classes so each published band is disjoint, and publishes conditions/drought.json.

From NYNJTC's public AGOL org 'nynjtc' (org id G1WTEJ6UVRUTvh9C). Registered by hand: discover_sources.py walks ATC's Experience Builder app and this org is not behind it.
sources.notes: 12 section features, measured live 2026-08-24 - again matching NYC_SOURCE_SURVEY.md §4's 2026-08-18 reading. Fields Trail_Name/Section_Name/Source/MapOrder; all 12 rows read Trail_Name 'Highlands' and Source 'NYNJTC', and Section_Name is a per-section label ('NJ 2'..'NJ 9' among the sampled twelve). dataLastEditDate verified live 2026-08-24, then reading 2025-12-04T21:03:02Z - eight months older than the Long Path's, which is what the survey meant by 'thinner'. THIS LAYER PUBLISHES NO BLAZE AT ALL: there is no blaze field, so blaze_default 'Unknown' states that absence rather than asserting a paint. That is deliberate and is the omit-rather-than-guess rule applied to a colour - the Highlands Trail does wear a blaze on the ground, and this pipeline has read it from no source it registered, so painting one here would be a display outrunning its source. What would settle it: the same NYNJTC conversation the licence waits on, or a blaze field appearing in one of the seasonal republishes this service does in place.

sources.title: NYNJTC Trail Alerts
sources.licence: See nynjtc_notices_licence below. Registered 2026-08-27 as unsettled and authorised by the maintainer the same day; what ships is the conservative facts-and-a-link split ATC's notices already ship on - title, locality, NYNJTC's own date and a link to their page, never their body text. NYNJTC's own terms remain the ideal and the ask is still open (https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/768).

freshness.notes: The category's RSS feed, used as a change signal and NOT as the content - the same division `atc_trail_updates` uses, and for the same reason: measured 2026-08-27 the feed held 12 items while the API held all 18, so building from it would silently drop six alerts. It is a BETTER marker than ATC's on both counts that matter. The validator is STRONG (`"b04bf0f8..."`, no `W/` prefix) where ATC's is weak, so a change to the bytes cannot leave the tag standing; and a `Last-Modified` is served beside it (Wed, 26 Aug 2026 21:41:57 GMT), giving check_freshness.py a second marker if the first is ever dropped. NYNJTC also does not refuse a scripted request the way ATC's host refuses the literal `python-requests/*` User-Agent - verified 2026-08-27 with urllib's default agent, which answered 200 - so nothing here depends on naming ourselves. fetch_nynjtc_alerts.py names the project anyway, as courtesy rather than necessity.

sources.discovered_via: pipeline/ALERTS_NOTICES_SURVEY.md §5b - the alerts survey #1073 ran across every org whose trails this build draws. Registered by hand: discover_sources.py walks ATC's Experience Builder app and this is a WordPress category, not a layer.
sources.notes: Fetched by fetch_nynjtc_alerts.py to data/raw/nynjtc_alerts.json (never by fetch_all.py, which fetches ArcGIS layers only) and exported by export_nynjtc_alerts.py to conditions/nynjtc_alerts.json, which publish.py uploads. WHAT `reaches_hikers: true` MEANS HERE, stated because this source reached it by a different road from every other one: an exporter reads it and its rows reach a release, which is the field's definition (reaches_hikers_comment). Every row ships in the WEAKEST form the design allows - `place: unplaced`, `obstructs_trail: false`, `review_state: unreviewed` - because reference/notice_places.json does not exist yet and nobody has reviewed NYNJTC's page. So the map draws none of these and the client surfaces them as a list a hiker reads, which is features/ORG_NOTICES.md §3's first-class unplaced state rather than a gap. 18 alerts on 2026-08-27, published 2024-01-11 to 2026-06-16, read from the WordPress REST API - `/wp-json/wp/v2/posts?categories=6` - rather than scraped, which is the whole difference from `atc_trail_updates`: there is no markup to misread, and `per_page`/`modified_after`/`_fields` are query parameters rather than things to reimplement. THE FIND THE SURVEY ITSELF MISSED, corrected in §5b the same day: NYNJTC tags each alert from its own CLOSED taxonomies, so placement is a join against tens of terms rather than a fuzzy match of prose against the 21,805 exported network features. Coverage measured on those 18 - park on 17, trail on 10, region and state on 7 each - and the trail vocabulary is 45 terms, the park vocabulary 125. That last number is why the fetcher pages every list route: `park` answers exactly 100 to a single per_page=100 request, and a vocabulary truncated there would drop placements with no error anywhere. ONE HYGIENE WART, recorded so it is not mistaken for a parser bug: `highlands-trail` is a term in BOTH the trail and park taxonomies (ids 31 and 405), so a join table must key on `taxonomy:slug` and never on the slug alone. features/ORG_NOTICES.md is the delivery design and holds the placement, dedup and voice questions; none of them is settled by this registration.

sources.foot_allowed_comment: WHAT `M` IN THE FOOT COLUMN IS READ AS, because dec_hiking_trails' foot_allowed keeps those 1,236 rows and the reading is ours rather than DEC's. DEC's CORRIDOR USE domain declares five codes with these labels, read off the live field metadata 2026-08-25: Y=YES, N=NO, U=UNDECIDED, M=MAINTAINED, -99=NO JURISDICTION. `M` is read here as 'DEC maintains this corridor for foot travel', which is at least as strong a statement about walkability as Y. @unvalidated - DEC publishes no data dictionary this project has found that defines the code per row, so the reading rests on the domain's own label plus what the rows look like: measured 2026-08-25, 991 of the 1,236 M rows are ASSET 'FOOT TRAIL', 681 carry a trail-marker colour, and the named ones are ordinary hiking trails (Bog Meadow Trail, the Finger Lakes Trail, the North Country Trail, the Long Path). What would settle it: DEC's own documentation of the CORRIDOR USE matrix, or the same conversation open_question above names. What the alternative costs: a foot_allowed of ['Y'] alone drops 23% of the layer DEC itself publishes as hiking trails, including named through-trails - a hiking-only filter deleting hiking trails, which is the wrong way for this to fail.
sources.discovered_via: pipeline/NYC_SOURCE_SURVEY.md §3's verdict - 'register next', written 2026-08-18 from the maintainer's own lead (gisservices.dec.ny.gov/gis/dil/, 'Outdoor Activity') - acted on under #1019, whose scope decision is what made a Catskills source non-optional. Registered by hand: this is an on-prem ArcGIS server rather than an AGOL org, so there is no item to discover and discover_sources.py has nothing to walk.
sources.notes: 5,286 polyline segments (4,931 LineString, 355 MultiLineString), fetched whole and counted 2026-08-25 - against the 5,277 NYC_SOURCE_SURVEY.md §3 read on 2026-08-11, so the layer moves. Fields UNIT/FACILITY/NAME/ASSET/MILES/DESCRIP/PUBLICUSE/UPDATED plus the per-use CORRIDOR USE matrix (FOOT/HORSE/BIKE/XC/SNOWMB/ATV/MOTORV/ADMIN/ACCESSIBLE/MAPPWD) and MARKER, which DEC aliases 'Trail Marker Color' and is this pipeline's blaze. FOUR THINGS A READER SHOULD NOT HAVE TO RE-FETCH TO LEARN. (1) MARKER is a genuine coded domain whose codes ARE the words (Red/Yellow/Blue/Orange/Green/White/Other), like oprhp_trails' Blaze and unlike side_trails' integers, so no domain decode stands in front of reference/blaze_mapping.json; live values on the 5,286 rows are 2,929 blank or null, Yellow 704, Blue 692, Red 622, White 128, Other 97, Orange 78, Green 35, and one 'ORANGE AND RED' that DEC's own domain does not declare. (2) FOOT reads Y on 4,050 rows and M on 1,236, and nothing else - see foot_allowed and foot_allowed_comment above. (3) THERE IS NO STATUS COLUMN, so every kept row exports as open under export_nearby_trails.py's DEFAULT_STATUS: DEC publishes no closure state here, and inventing one would be the failure that module's closure treatment exists to avoid. PUBLICUSE reads 'Y' on all 5,286, which is a layer-wide constant rather than a filter worth having. (4) IDS FALL BACK TO OBJECTID, because DEC spells the column GLOBALID and lib/feature_id.py looks for GlobalID - the ids are unique across the fetched 5,286 and stable within a fetch, but a DEC republish that renumbers OBJECTIDs would renumber ours; the stable column is there for the taking if that ever bites. FRESHNESS: no editingInfo (a classic on-prem MapServer), so fetch_external_layers.py's change-aware skip cannot fire for this entry and it is re-fetched every run - accepted rather than fixed, because the layer is 13 MB and the alternative is machinery nothing else needs. The marker the survey identified does work and costs one request: max(UPDATED) via outStatistics answered in 0.5 s on 2026-08-25 and returned 2026-08-20. THE LAYER'S OWN SCOPE, stated because the name oversells it: 'Hiking Trails' is DEC's per-use split, so a row is here because foot travel is allowed on it, not because it is a footpath - 446 rows are ASSET 'SNOWMOBILE TRAIL' with FOOT 'Y', 456 are unpaved roads, and they are walkable corridors on DEC land rather than mistakes. UNIT mixes preserve codes (AFP 2,293, CFP 312) with hundreds of per-county state-forest codes and some dirt (blank, misspellings), exactly as the survey warned; nothing filters on it, per #1019.

oprhp_licence._comment: The basis on which the four oprhp_* layers above may be fetched, and the bar their data has to clear before any of it is republished to hikers. CORRECTED 2026-08-24 (#950). This block previously said OPRHP's terms were UNSTATED and that the item's licenseInfo was 'a no-warranty disclaimer'. THAT WAS WRONG, and the way it was wrong is worth recording: the licenseInfo was read through a 200-character truncation on 2026-08-18, which cut off exactly at the sentence where the disclaimer ends and the actual terms begin. The full field is 1,095 characters of plain text on AGOL item a89dcd37f8bc41929e490dacd872e288 (the item whose `url` is the registered NY_State_Parks_Trails FeatureServer), re-read in full 2026-08-24 and quoted verbatim in `terms_verbatim` below. SO THERE IS A GRANT, WITH TWO CONDITIONS ON IT. Reuse is permitted; attribution to OPRHP is REQUIRED on 'any maps, reports, or other materials created using OPRHP data'; and the data is provided 'for informational and NON-COMMERCIAL purposes'. The second condition is the one that needs a human: features/PRICING_MODEL.md designs a paid thru-hike pass and regional passes, so whether shipping these lines inside OurHike is a non-commercial use is a judgement about the product, not a fact about the layer. The reading that says yes is PRICING_MODEL.md's own pricing value #5 - the trail line is in the tier that 'stay[s] free forever, for everyone, regardless of ability to pay', and what is sold is the convenience layer above it. That reading is not recorded here as settled, because nobody with authority to settle it has written it down.

oprhp_licence.basis: OPRHP's own published item terms (read 2026-08-24, quoted verbatim above), plus the maintainer's determination of the same date that OurHike is a non-commercial use within them. THE REASONING, recorded because a determination nobody can inspect is worth no more than an assertion: features/PRICING_MODEL.md's pricing value #1 keeps the core map, water, shelters, GPS, elevation, closures and warnings 'free forever, for everyone, regardless of ability to pay', and a trail line is squarely in that tier. What OurHike sells is the planning and community layer above it - value #5's 'a maintained, polished experience on top of open data'. So OPRHP's data itself is given to hikers for nothing. THE COUNTER-READING, stated so nobody has to reconstruct it: the app as a whole does take money, and a stricter reading of 'non-commercial purposes' looks at the product rather than at the tier. reaches_hikers_comment: Why every source entry carries `reaches_hikers` (#927). The sources screen names the organizations whose data is on a hiker's phone, under the terms each one set - so it has to know which registered sources actually SHIP, and that fact lived only in prose inside each entry's `licence` string ('fetched for REVIEW AND CROSS-CHECKS ONLY', 'nothing from this source reaches a published artifact until...'). A screen that decided by reading those sentences would print a licence claim for data nobody publishes the first time one was reworded. So it is a field: true means an exporter reads this source and its data reaches a release, false means registered-but-not-shipped, for any reason - review-only pending a licence answer (gatc_water_sources, every oprhp_*), watched-only (usgs_3dhp), or registered and not yet wired to anything (bridges, at_treadway, per pipeline/README.md). It is NOT a licence judgement and does not replace one: a source can be freely licensed and still not ship. export_sources.py refuses to run if any entry lacks the field, so a newly registered source cannot reach a hiker's screen by defaulting into it.
